body.x: Amid CES 2026, the world’s largest technology exhibition, the Global Innovation Forum (GIF 2026) was held in Las Vegas, drawing global attention as a rare platform where startup pitching and cross-national startup cooperation converged on a single stage.

Hosted by the Seoul Business Agency (SBA), the forum took place on January 7 (local time), the second day of CES 2026, at the Emperors Ballroom of Caesars Palace. GIF 2026 stood out as the only global startup pitching event during CES officially joined by multiple national startup support organizations, positioning itself at the very center of the exhibition’s global innovation ecosystem.

CES 2026 served as a high-density global arena where investors, innovative companies, and decision-makers gathered in unprecedented concentration. With approximately 53% of CES participants identified as executive-level decision-makers, startup pitching during this period functioned not as a separate IR event, but as the market itself—where audiences, media, and venture capital naturally intersected. Within this environment, GIF 2026 operated as a platform for the most realistic validation of startup value.

body.x: “Innovators Show Up” Comes to Life at CES 2026

The forum aligned closely with CES 2026’s official theme, “Innovators Show Up.” Rather than focusing solely on technical explanations, the event highlighted a shift to a new era in which founders and leaders must step onto the stage themselves and demonstrate judgment, strategy, and conviction.

The GIF 2026 IR pitching stage featured eight startups representing seven countries—Korea, France, Japan, Taiwan, Israel, Canada, and Switzerland. Each startup was directly selected by its national startup support organization, forming a structure in which technology, business models, and global scalability were evaluated simultaneously under global standards.

Participating startups represented key CES 2026 technology trends, including AI and robotics, digital health, mobility, battery and energy, and spatial and photonics technologies. Their presentations emphasized global expansion strategies, business models, and investment readiness rather than technical demonstrations alone. In CES’s high-pressure decision-making environment, pitching immediately led to direct feedback and follow-up discussions, reinforcing its role as a live market engagement.

body.cap: Following the IR pitching sessions, global media outlets including Forbes conduct on-site interviews with participating startups and stakeholders. Pitching outcomes translated simultaneously into investment consideration and global exposure. | Photo – AVING News

body.x: Judging was conducted by 25 venture capitalists and global accelerator representatives based in the United States, Korea, and Europe. Institutions such as Plug and Play Korea participated, applying a practical evaluation framework focused on market viability, team capability, and investment suitability. The structure was designed to facilitate post-pitch investment reviews and follow-up meetings rather than simple ranking.

This approach distinguished GIF 2026 from conventional pitching competitions. The evaluation process itself functioned as a first meeting between startups and investors, with immediate Q&A and discussions following each presentation. The emphasis was placed on long-term connectivity and expansion potential rather than short-term outcomes.

Global media presence further amplified the forum’s impact. More than 100 journalists and influencers from over 20 countries, including representatives from Forbes, Digitimes, and Innovation & Tech Today, attended the event. As a result, pitching outcomes translated simultaneously into investment consideration and global exposure. GIF 2026 was widely recognized as a practical global startup stage where evaluation, media coverage, and connection operated concurrently.

body.x: "From Player to Architect: Korea’s Evolving Role"

Beyond individual startup outcomes, GIF 2026 also symbolized the evolution of Korea’s startup policy. Korea has long been recognized for its world-class startup support infrastructure. However, GIF 2026 demonstrated a shift beyond being a strong “supporting nation” toward becoming a designer of global startup ecosystems—connecting countries, structuring collaboration, and orchestrating shared platforms.

The IR pitching competition stood at the center of this transformation. Unlike closed IR rooms or limited investor-only presentations, CES itself functioned as a natural point of contact. Startups engaged immediately with global VCs, media, and industry stakeholders, extending discussions well beyond the stage.

Following the pitching sessions, panel discussions featuring national startup support organizations explored global startup trends and country-specific support strategies. These discussions served not only as knowledge-sharing sessions but also as checkpoints for cross-national policy collaboration. Subsequent networking sessions enabled startups, investors, media, and ecosystem operators to pursue tangible business opportunities.

Representatives of First Habit, winner of the Grand Award at the Global Innovation Forum (GIF 2026) IR Pitching Competition, pose for a commemorative photo holding the trophy and prize. | Photo – AVING News

body.x: After the IR pitching sessions, panel discussions featuring representatives from participating countries followed. The sessions shared the latest trends in the global startup ecosystem and country-specific startup support strategies, serving as a platform to review cross-national policy alignment and collaboration models beyond the growth of individual companies. The networking sessions that followed allowed startups, venture capitalists (VCs), media, and startup support organizations to interact freely and explore tangible business opportunities.

At the event, startups that demonstrated innovation and global scalability through the IR pitching sessions were presented with the Grand Award, Scale-up Award, and Impact Award. The Grand Award was presented to First Habit for its lifestyle and consumer behavior analytics–based solution, while the Scale-up Award went to HUA TECH INTERNATIONAL, recognized for its potential in technology commercialization and global business expansion. The Impact Award, which evaluates social value and applied technology potential, was awarded to Cubic Space, a company specializing in spatial technology solutions.

The award-winning companies were praised for clearly demonstrating scalability, market viability, and execution capability—key themes of CES 2026—across diverse technology sectors. Notably, the awards represented more than a simple ranking outcome; they reflected the results of a practical, globally validated evaluation jointly conducted by international investors, media, and startup support organizations. The IR pitching stage of GIF 2026 thus functioned not only as an awards platform, but as a starting point for each company’s next phase of global engagement.

Meanwhile, the forum’s most significant achievement extended beyond the awards themselves. The greater meaning lay in Korea’s leadership in designing a unified global startup stage and validating that model on the world’s largest technology platform—CES.
